submissionAttempts.body:
Ordering guarantee = GLOBAL: the state-change feed exposes one monotonic, durable commit-observation order shared by every reader of the store (a single, filter-independent cursor position). Record A (09-ordering-contract-a.md) is the operative record; Record B's "per-consumer ordering" is not supported by the current pinned line.

Why this was the decision:
1. Conflict identified. Two unindexed engineering records both claim "normative, current pinned line" with opposite guarantees: A = global (one position shared by all readers); B = per-consumer (each consumer an independent position). Neither is listed in docs/engineering/README.md (which lists 09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md as doc 09), and neither claims version/temporal precedence over the other, so provenance/index alone cannot pick one.
2. Authority rule. Per PLMP-ALN-1 (07-ordarium-alignment.md §0/§2), the reconciliation authority says Ordarium's kernel contract is owned on the Ordarium side (its docs/12-17, ORD-BOOT-0), and this workspace consumes it only through public, pinned artifacts. The two records are both Palimpsest-side interface records for an Ordarium-owned contract, so the pinned contract is the deciding evidence.
3. Pinned-artifact evidence (actual install = 1.3.1, per package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides + node_modules):
   - @ordarium/core 1.3.1 types.d.ts: cursor is the "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; changes are delivered "in durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending"; a consumer reaching the end still holds one durable resume position.
   - @ordarium/core 1.3.1 ledger.js (MemoryLedger): a single #stateChanges array where "element i is the commit at position i + 1"; changes() walks one global position sequence and fails closed (InvalidCursorError) for a position beyond the ledger's highest commit.
   - @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 index.js: "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; validation is against the global high-water mark MAX(change_seq); reading is ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC over a single ordarium_state_changes(change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) table.
   - @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 migrations.js (v3->v4, ORD-BOOT-0 §7): "v3 recorded no global commit order... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order." A single global sequence is the explicit design intent.
4. Consequence for the integration: consumers may each persist their own cursor value, but that value indexes the one shared global position - it does not create a per-consumer ordering (the cursor is filter-independent and validated against the global mark). Actually, Palimpsest's sole state-kind surface (PalimpsestEffectsRuntime.state, createStateStore in src/effects/runtime.ts) consumes list/CAS, not changes(), so the global feed order is a shared-ledger contract property rather than a current Palimpsest resume mechanism; the telemetry append-delta/commutative-sum design (PLMP-TLM-1) is deliberately order-insensitive and remains consistent with it.
5. No peer escalation was required: the collaboration inbox was empty, and the conflict is decidable from the pinned Ordarium artifact, so it was not a case of unresolved load-bearing sources where the peer owns a missing resolution.

Recommended follow-up (local, not part of this disposition): remove or correct 09-ordering-contract-b.md so the archive no longer carries a contradictory normative ordering record, and add the ordering record(s) to the docs/engineering index.

Ordering guarantee (best-supported reading): GLOBAL - the state-change feed exposes one monotonic, durable commit-observation order shared by all readers; the cursor is a single, filter-independent position. Record A (09-ordering-contract-a.md) matches the pinned line; Record B (per-consumer independent ordering, 09-ordering-contract-b.md) contradicts it.

Evidence (pinned line = ordarium-v1.3.1, per package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides + installed node_modules):
- @ordarium/core 1.3.1 types.d.ts: StateChangePage.cursor is "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; changes delivered "in durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending".
- @ordarium/core 1.3.1 ledger.js (MemoryLedger): single #stateChanges array, "element i is the commit at position i + 1"; InvalidCursorError past the highest commit.
- @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 index.js: "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; validation against MAX(change_seq); ordarium_state_changes(change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT), ORDER BY change_seq ASC.
- @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 migrations.js v3->v4 (ORD-BOOT-0 §7): "v3 recorded no global commit order... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."

Authority boundary: the two records are mutually exclusive "normative, current scope" sources, neither indexed nor superseded locally, and per PLMP-ALN-1 the ordering contract is owned by the Ordarium side (docs/12-17, ORD-BOOT-0). I therefore opened thread "state-change-feed-ordering", posted a question + need, and proposed contract "state-change-feed-ordering" (revision 1, termsDigest 4a03e555...) to establish the authority-participation basis. As of this submission the contract is still draft (acceptedBy empty) and no authoritative reply has arrived; the earlier submission was rejected with UNRESOLVED_LOAD_BEARING_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY.

If an accepted authoritative ruling is required before this can be admitted as resolved, this submission should be treated as the provisional reading and the open authority step is: ordarium.main accepts/revises the contract and cites the anchor.
